narrative.overview: Blueprint Studio is a rigorous planning tool built like a well-made 8-bit game. Every panel is a chunky pixel frame, headings are set in pixel type, and one green "go" colour marks the action that moves the session forward. The game language serves the work: it makes a long, structured interview feel like progress through levels, while the data itself (item IDs, quotes, tokens, tickets) stays in a calm monospace that reads like a spec. The system ships as three themes the user picks in Settings, each a full peer: 8-bit Day, 8-bit Night and High-Contrast Terminal. Density is Operate-grade; the arcade lives in frames, type and the sky, never in the content.
keyCharacteristics: Square corners everywhere; depth comes from stepped, hard-edged pixel shadows, never blur.
One accent (`accent-go`) shared by all three themes, used as a fill for the primary action, the current selection and "healthy" marks.
Three type voices: pixel display (Pixelify Sans), pixel labels (Silkscreen) and monospace data (JetBrains Mono).
Pixel icons drawn on a 16-unit grid with crisp edges.
Motion is stepped, like sprite frames, and stops entirely under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Go Rule
rules.body: Go Green appears once per decision: the primary action, the current selection, or a healthy mark. If two green fills compete on one panel, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Fill-Not-Ink Rule
rules.body: Bright Go Green is never text on a light surface. On Day, green text uses Go Green Ink; on the dark themes, text sitting on a green fill uses the darkest ink.

rules.name: The Stepped Gradient Rule
rules.body: Skies are banded in hard stops, like a palette-limited sprite. Smooth gradients don't exist in this system.

rules.name: The Data Stays Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything the user wrote, approved or will export (item IDs, quotes, requirements, ticket text) is set in JetBrains Mono. Pixel faces never carry content.

rules.name: The Label Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Silkscreen is for labels of a few words. Never set a sentence in it.

rules.name: The No-Blur Rule
rules.body: Every shadow has zero blur and zero spread. A soft shadow breaks the world.

rules.name: The Notched Corner Rule
rules.body: Frames are drawn with four single-axis offsets so the corners stay notched. Never use a plain `border` on an 8-bit surface.

dos: **Do** frame every 8-bit surface with the four-offset pixel frame and keep a 2–3px margin outside it.
**Do** keep Go Green a fill. Use `accent-go-ink` for green text on Day.
**Do** set every ID, quote and requirement in JetBrains Mono, and keep labels in Silkscreen to a few words.
**Do** step every animation (`steps()` timing) and stop all of it under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** keep the Night sky quiet and behind content: no star, constellation or comet may cross text or controls.
**Do** give every status chip an icon and a label as well as its colour.
**Do** put the Day · Night · Contrast switcher in the header of every screen, linking to the same screen in each theme.
**Do** meet WCAG 2.1 AA in all three themes; check Day's faint text (`day-faint` on white) and Night's faint text (`night-faint` on `night-panel`) whenever a surface changes.
donts: **Don't** round a corner, blur a shadow or use a smooth gradient.
**Don't** add a second accent hue. Status colours are reserved for status and never decorate.
**Don't** set a sentence or user content in a pixel face.
**Don't** treat Terminal as a fallback: it is an equal theme and gets the same polish and the same screens.
**Don't** bring back the rejected directions (Dark IDE, Dither Mono, Tactical HUD, Minimalist Ledger) or the brief's banned faces (Inter, Arial).
**Don't** use purple-to-blue gradients, glossy blobs or rounded SaaS card shadows.
